summary: Yukio Yamanaka works in Indology and linguistics. He studied as a graduate student at Kyoto University (attested 1996) and held a post as a DFG Research Fellow at the University of Göttingen (attested 2015).
Yuko Kamishima is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied at the University of Tokyo and under Ekai Kawaguchi as a research student, later holding a post at Ritsumeikan University.
Yuko Matsuda is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied at Aoyama Gakuin Women's Junior College and held a post at Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College (attested 2001).

Yuko Yokochi is an Indologist who studied at the University of Tokyo (MA) under Minoru Hara and Katsuhiko Kamimura, and earned a PhD at the University of Groningen in 2004. She was an Associate Professor (attested 2002) and Professor (attested 2012–2021) at Kyoto University.

Yukteshwar Kumar is a sinologist who studied at Visva-Bharati University, Peking University, and Jawaharlal Nehru University (~1993–2003) under Tan Chung. He held posts at the University of Delhi, Jawaharlal Nehru University, and the University of Bath (~2012).
Yulian Zeng is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University (attested 2010) under the supervision of Kirill Jurievitch Solonin.
Yumi Katayama specializes in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. She was a PhD student at Hiroshima University (attested 2007) and studied under Kenyu Mitomo (attested 2013).

Yumi Nakamoto works in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. At Ryukoku University, she was a research student (attested 2014), a researcher (2012), and a graduate research student (attested 2014).
Yumiko Ishihama works in Tibetology, history/archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Waseda University (~1980–1989) and later held a post there (~1997).

Yun Ji is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned a PhD in Chinese literature from Fudan University in 2006 and served as an assistant professor at the Buddhist College of Singapore (attested 2015).

Yun-hua Jan was a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies who studied under Yun-shan Tan. He served as a Research Fellow at Visva-Bharati University (1953) and as a Professor at McMaster University (attested 1984–1990).

Yun-shan Tan worked in sinology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. Educated at Wenjiang Shuyuan, Mijiang Academy, Chuanshan Academy, and Hunan Normal University (-1919), he studied under Lan-Chi Chen, Ziyuan Long, Taixu, and Kshitimohan Sen. He taught at Lida Academy and Visva-Bharati University.
Yungfen Ma is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. She completed a PhD at Columbia University, where she studied under Chun-fang Yu (attested 2011).
Yusen Kashiwahara was a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He studied at Otani University and later served as a professor there (~1950–1987).

Yusho Miyasaka studied Buddhist studies and Indology at Tohoku University (~1945–1948). He served as an associate professor at Koyasan University (~1956–1974), held a post at Shuchiin University, and was named Professor Emeritus at Nagoya University in 1976.

Yusho Wakahara specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Ryukoku University under Eshō Mikogami, lecturing at Hanazono University (attested 1987), and served at Ryukoku University as an associate professor (attested 1987–1999) and professor (attested 2011–2013).
Yutai Ikeda was a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts at Otani University and Doho University, where he was an Emeritus Professor (attested 2006).

Yutaka Hirata was a scholar of history/archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at Kyushu University (~1950–1955), served on the faculty of Nagasaki Junshin Catholic University, and became Professor Emeritus at Kyushu University (~1995–2013).

Yutaka Iwamoto specialized in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University (~1933–1936) under Toru Haneda, Hidenaka Tanaka, Atsuuji Ashikaga, Naoshiro Tsuji, and Gyoyu Tokiwai. He held posts at Kyoto Tachibana University (~1967–1981) and Soka University (~1981–1988).
Yutaka Kawasaki is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied under Seio Okuda. He held a post at the University of Tokyo (attested 2024).
